note: In-session exercise: participant works through a 5-4-3-2-1 grounding exercise, states benefit, and agrees to use it on a named occasion.
turns: Hi. How are you right now?
Honestly kind of panicky. I just got off the bus and it was packed and I felt like I couldn't get air. My hands are still shaking.
That sounds frightening. Would you like to try a grounding exercise with me right now?
Look around and tell me five things you can see.
Okay. My desk lamp. A blue mug. The window. My backpack on the floor. A poster of a mountain.
Good. Now four things you can touch.
The chair under me. My jeans. The edge of the desk, it's cold. My phone.
The fridge humming. Someone's music through the wall. My own breathing I guess.
And take one slow breath in, and a long breath out. How is your body now?
Slower. My hands stopped shaking. I can actually feel my feet on the floor.
Well done. Would you be willing to use this the next time it happens on the bus?
Yes. Next time I'm on the bus and it starts, I'll do the five things I can see. I'll try it on Thursday's ride.
That really worked, I feel a lot calmer than ten minutes ago. Thank you.
